items.proposed_content: The unit supports a three-way proof-status audit. The self-approximation inequality (9.3) is proved for every irrational d and for reduced nonzero rational d=a/b when |a-b| is not 1; earlier claims covering every nonzero rational had a gap, and the repaired statement leaves |a-b|=1 uncovered without declaring those cases false. For log ζ, the earlier argument is reported valid for every nonzero real d. Changing from ζ to log ζ therefore changes the proved parameter range, but the source does not explain the mechanism; d=0 remains only a hypothetical log-ζ statement whose validity would imply RH.

items.proposed_content: Ordinary universality of zeta is restricted to nonvanishing targets, whereas strong universality for the stated Hurwitz cases allows targets with zeros; Rouché's theorem then converts positive-density approximation of a linear target into linearly many zeros. For zeta, which cannot be strongly universal in the strip, approximation of zeta by its own shifts is the compatible recurrence statement and is equivalent to RH.

items.proposed_content: Universality and joint universality can fail when algebraic or arithmetic relations confine the orbit: sparse Dirichlet support can collapse a series to a nonuniversal rational function, inversion identities can prevent joint density, and resonances in discrete shifts or scaled self-approximation require exclusions or modified Euler products.

items.proposed_content: The visible scope of a universality theorem changes with its analytic input: available mean values delimit strips, coefficient moments can replace pointwise assumptions, prime-geodesic error exponents determine a strip, a lower-depth nonzero value is an explicit hypothesis in a one-variable multiple-zeta theorem, and effective approximation tools turn qualitative recurrence into numerical density and first-hit bounds.

items.proposed_content: Universality transports through a construction when targets can be encoded or pulled back to admissible inputs and the construction preserves approximation control: disjoint translated compacts encode several shift targets into one target, hybrid joint universality controls coefficients and phases for combinations, and composite operators use preimages plus stability bounds to propagate approximation error.

items.proposed_content: The survey organizes universality as orbit visitation at several resolutions: point and derivative-value density lift to function-space approximation; general orbit closure includes both vertical translation and torus rotation; weighted averages, ergodic iterates, and random paths change the clock or sampling measure used to count visits; zeta self-recurrence is a special orbit statement equivalent to RH.
